deltas.rationale: docs/runbooks/release.md §6, core 0047 row: 0047 lets a governance field of a published Operation change only together with the operation.governance_refreshed AuditRecord stating the new values, in the same transaction. The previous release's product path writes that record: its refresh_operation_governance handler writes it after refreshOperationGovernance's in-place write, in the same transaction, so a code-only rollback keeps working. These three tests call refreshOperationGovernance directly, without the handler, so the previous release writes no record and the commit is refused by design. HEAD's refreshOperationGovernance writes the record itself, and the same tests pass in HEAD; the replacements assert the record and the refusal.

deltas.rationale: docs/runbooks/release.md §6, governance 0036 row (conditionally reversible): 0036 adds the guard admin_proposal_segments_target_chosen — a workspace segment of an admin proposal is written, and moves to applied, only while its target is among the targets its proposer chose for their admin agent in that trial workspace (admin_agent_targets; the AA4c plan's F5 and D1). v0.61.0 has no targets: its admin agent may propose to any active standard workspace, so on this schema every admin proposal of its with a workspace segment is refused — all of the BASE failures below are that one refusal ("the workspace segment's target is not among its proposer's targets"), raised while the test makes its proposal, and each asserts the rule 0036 changes on purpose. This is a behaviour change for a code-only rollback, not a test artefact alone: v0.61.0's own propose path is refused the same way, so code may roll back only after dropping that trigger and its function (0036 header; the §6 row says so). The admin agent is off by default (ADMIN_AGENT_ENABLED), so a deployment that never enabled it never reaches the guard. HEAD's versions of these tests choose the targets first, as the platform's admin agent page does; the replacements assert the new rule: targets are chosen per person and trial workspace, a target not chosen is refused with one code on every channel, a target dropped later blocks its segment until it is chosen again, and the guard holds for a write that does not come from the kernel.
